resources.name: Agent Deck
resources.description: A Mac interface for coding agent sessions, project context and skills.
resources.for_whom: Developers coordinating coding sessions.
resources.access_notes: Sessions may run tools with access to local files and connected services.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Hunk
resources.description: A terminal interface for reviewing code changes with agent notes beside the diff.
resources.for_whom: Developers reviewing agent generated changes.
resources.access_notes: Review changes before applying them; installation and repository access are separate decisions.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Jevgrep
resources.description: Search a codebase with a question and receive relevant files and source excerpts.
resources.for_whom: Coding agents and developers exploring an unfamiliar repository.
resources.access_notes: Requires an AI provider connection; check what repository content is sent to that provider.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Needle
resources.description: Models and runtimes for local tool calling, structured extraction and embeddings.
resources.for_whom: Developers building applications on devices.
resources.access_notes: Your application defines and executes the tools; constrain their permissions.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Are you found by AI? MCP server
resources.description: Connect an MCP client to saved AI visibility measurements and evidence.
resources.for_whom: Businesses and agencies using their own AI to inspect visibility data.
resources.access_notes: Account access is scoped by the connection. Review the rescan action separately from read tools.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: gogcli
resources.description: A command line interface for Google Workspace services with structured output.
resources.for_whom: People and agents automating Workspace tasks.
resources.access_notes: OAuth scopes can allow reads and writes. Choose the account and access needed for the task.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: CISO AI
resources.description: Security briefings, analysis and governance resources.
resources.for_whom: Teams following security developments and governance topics.
resources.access_notes: Read the linked primary sources and check dates before using advice in an operational decision.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: node9
resources.description: Access control for AI agents. It decides what Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor and MCP servers may do, and can block or review risky actions.
resources.for_whom: People running coding agents against Slack, GitHub, email, files or databases.
resources.access_notes: Install with brew tap node9-ai/node9 && brew install node9, or npm install -g node9-ai. Needs Node.js 22 or later. Local protection needs no account. Optional dashboard login. Apache-2.0.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: ClawSecCheck
resources.description: A local, read-only security audit for an OpenClaw agent. It looks for config, prompt-injection and supply-chain risks and can vet a skill before install.
resources.for_whom: People running OpenClaw who want a local A to F grade without sending config off the machine.
resources.access_notes: Python 3.10 or later. Install with pipx from the GitHub repo. The scanner reports and does not change OpenClaw config. Official docs say the scanner makes no network calls. MIT.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: GuardStein
resources.description: A document and deal room service that describes browser encryption and controlled sharing.
resources.for_whom: Teams evaluating document sharing for deals and reviews.
resources.access_notes: Encryption claims are the provider's. Review its security model and recovery process before uploading sensitive documents.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Raft
resources.description: A shared workspace where people and persistent AI agents collaborate in messages and tasks.
resources.for_whom: Teams working with agents across projects and machines.
resources.access_notes: Source available under FSL, not an unrestricted open source licence. Agents need explicit access to their tools and data.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: x402
resources.description: An open protocol for payments over HTTP using the 402 response.
resources.for_whom: Developers building services that charge per request.
resources.access_notes: Connecting a payment client can spend funds. Set explicit transaction limits.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: THL Open
resources.description: Agent skills and reporting tools for AI readiness audits and fix plans.
resources.for_whom: Agencies, consultants and teams evaluating their own or authorised client sites.
resources.access_notes: Skills may use external services or scan a site. Obtain target permission and review dependencies before running them.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Official MCP Registry
resources.description: The official hosted registry of publicly available Model Context Protocol servers, with a REST API and server.json metadata.
resources.for_whom: MCP clients, aggregators and people looking up a server by name.
resources.access_notes: The registry is in preview. Breaking changes or data resets may occur before general availability. Listing a server is not a security audit. Installing a listed server still needs its own credentials and terms.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: OmniRoute
resources.description: A local AI gateway that routes coding tools to many provider accounts through one OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
resources.for_whom: People who already have provider accounts and want one local endpoint with fallback.
resources.access_notes: Install with npm install -g omniroute. It runs locally (default http://localhost:20128). Bring your own provider credentials. OmniRoute does not grant tokens. MIT.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: GitHub MCP Server
resources.description: GitHub's official MCP server for repositories, issues, pull requests and Actions.
resources.for_whom: Agents and developers working on GitHub data they are allowed to access.
resources.access_notes: Needs a GitHub OAuth login or personal access token. Scopes can read and write repositories. Use a read-only token unless a write is required.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: GitMCP
resources.description: A remote MCP server that turns a public GitHub project into documentation an agent can query.
resources.for_whom: People pointing an agent at a public repository without cloning it.
resources.access_notes: Works on public GitHub content. Last upstream push observed 2026-05-08. Confirm the target repo is public before connecting.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: XERJ
resources.description: A local-first search engine and MCP server that indexes code, docs, logs and PDFs for agents.
resources.for_whom: People who want cited local search and agent memory without a hosted search cluster.
resources.access_notes: Installer is curl -fsSL https://xerj.org/get | sh. Read the script before running it. The binary indexes local paths and can serve an Elasticsearch-compatible API on localhost. Apache-2.0.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: AGENTS.md
resources.description: An open markdown format at the root of a repository that tells coding agents how the project works.
resources.for_whom: Repository maintainers and coding agents.
resources.access_notes: A file in a clone. It does not grant credentials. Agents that read it will follow those instructions, so keep secrets out of it.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: npx skills
resources.description: A command line installer that copies Agent Skills (SKILL.md folders) into the skill directories of local coding agents.
resources.for_whom: People installing portable skills into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and similar agents.
resources.access_notes: Writes files onto the machine. Treat a skill as untrusted code and instructions until you have read it. Example: npx skills add techhorizonlabs/thl-open.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Anthropic skills
resources.description: Public Agent Skills from Anthropic for coding agents that read SKILL.md.
resources.for_whom: People installing first-party examples of the Agent Skills format.
resources.access_notes: Public git clone or npx skills add. GitHub licence field was empty on 26 October 2026. Read the repository licence files before reuse.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Firecrawl
resources.description: Crawl and scrape sites into markdown and structured data for agents.
resources.for_whom: Agents and developers who need page content from the public web.
resources.access_notes: The hosted API needs a key and spends credits. AGPL-3.0 on the open repository. Do not scrape sites that forbid it. LinkedIn and similar sites may be blocked.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: REA
resources.description: A local MCP and CLI for investigating application behaviour, from JavaScript bundles to native binaries.
resources.for_whom: Developers and coding agents inspecting software they are allowed to analyse.
resources.access_notes: Install with npx rea-agents@latest setup. Setup shows a plan and asks before writing agent config or installing Hopper. Native and runtime workflows can execute or attach to programs. DISCLAIMER.md forbids DRM circumvention and copying proprietary software. MIT. npm package rea-agents. MCP registry name io.github.morluto/rea.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: OpenCLI
resources.description: A CLI and Chrome Browser Bridge that lets agents navigate, click, fill forms and extract from sites through a logged-in Chrome profile.
resources.for_whom: People whose agents need to operate websites they are already signed into, or reuse site-specific CLI adapters.
resources.access_notes: Install npm package @jackwener/opencli (Node.js 20.18.1 or later) or the desktop app, plus the OpenCLI Chrome extension. Browser commands act through the signed-in Chrome profile, including cookies for the target site. Treat that as the same access the person has in the browser. Apache-2.0. Skills install with npx skills add jackwener/opencli.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Graphify
resources.description: Turns a codebase, docs, SQL schemas, configs and PDFs into a local queryable knowledge graph for coding agents.
resources.for_whom: People whose agents need a map of a repository without sending the tree to a hosted vector store.
resources.access_notes: Install the CLI with uv tool install graphifyy, then graphify install. It reads local project files and writes graphify-out. Apache-2.0.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: OpenContext
resources.description: A local GUI and CLI that stores project context, skills and notes so a coding agent can reuse them across sessions.
resources.for_whom: People who already run Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode and want a persistent memory for that work.
resources.access_notes: Install with npm install -g @aicontextlab/cli, then oc init in a project. Desktop app from GitHub releases. MIT.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Stash
resources.description: Captures agent runs and human corrections, then serves that history back as knowledge, skills, REST, MCP and a CLI.
resources.for_whom: Teams whose agents should remember lessons from earlier work.
resources.access_notes: Python client is pip install stash-sdk. It reads STASH_API_KEY and optional STASH_URL. The GitHub repo is MIT. Hosted and self-hosted paths are separate accounts.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Browsentic
resources.description: An agentic browser harness: a desktop app, npm CLI and Chrome or Firefox extension that lets an agent drive a signed-in browser.
resources.for_whom: People whose agents need to use the browser they already use, including logged-in sites.
resources.access_notes: Installer is curl -fsSL https://browsentic.com/install.sh | sh. Read the script before running it. Or npx browsentic@latest setup. The extension acts through the signed-in browser. Apache-2.0.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Trail-code
resources.description: A local map of a codebase plus team learnings, so coding agents go to the right files and pick up earlier decisions.
resources.for_whom: People running Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or similar on a repository they control.
resources.access_notes: Install with npm install -g @trailhq/trail-code && trail init. It reads the repo on the machine and writes .trail/. MIT.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: obsidian-wiki
resources.description: A local markdown vault an agent can grow, lint and query as a digital brain.
resources.for_whom: People who want durable notes an agent can read and write in a folder they own.
resources.access_notes: Install with pip install obsidian-wiki, then obsidian-wiki setup --vault ~/brain. MIT. The vault is local files.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: earshot
resources.description: A local CLI, Python API and MCP server that lets coding agents describe, score and generate sound on CPU.
resources.for_whom: People whose agents make or review audio, film or game sound without a GPU.
resources.access_notes: Python 3.10 or later and ffmpeg on PATH. Clone the repo, venv, CPU torch, then pip install -e ".[mcp,llm,dev]". First model use downloads about 1.1 GB into a local cache. MIT.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: PromptDirector
resources.description: A free local-first Chrome extension that saves images, prompts and references from the web for later reuse.
resources.for_whom: People collecting visual and prompt references while they browse.
resources.access_notes: Chrome Web Store listing iahakaahijddcjjldidbclicedibgpjm. Optional local video component. Apache-2.0. Treat saved pages as the same access the signed-in browser has.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Hyperresearch
resources.description: A deep research skill and CLI that collects web and scholarly sources into a persistent vault and writes a cited report.
resources.for_whom: People running long research jobs in Claude Code or Codex, or using the hosted site.
resources.access_notes: pip install writes skills, hooks and project files. Runs need network and write access. Hosted product at hyperresearch.ai is a separate account. MIT. Check what the vault stores before pointing it at private material.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Tech Horizon Academy
resources.description: A free academy of Claude skills, prompts and AI tools for Australian small businesses.
resources.for_whom: Australian operators and the agents they run.
resources.access_notes: Public site. Skills and prompts are instructions; tools in the directory may need their own accounts. Indexes on 27 Oct 2026: 67 skills, 206 tools, 1217 prompt titles. Indexes are names and notes, not skill bodies or prompt text. Some academy tool pages carry partner flags; Gearlist omits referral parameters.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Claude Academy
resources.description: Anthropic's official courses on Claude, Claude Code, MCP, skills and the Claude API.
resources.for_whom: People learning Claude products and MCP.
resources.access_notes: Free courses at academy.claude.com. Some lessons need a Claude account.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Claude plugins official
resources.description: Anthropic's official Claude Code plugin marketplace. 315 plugins counted on 27 Oct 2026, mostly partner connectors.
resources.for_whom: Claude Code users installing plugins with /plugin.
resources.access_notes: Claude Code adds this marketplace on first interactive session. A plugin can install MCP servers and write config. Review a plugin before enabling it. Names and homepages are in indexes/claude-plugins-official.json. Not a security audit of each plugin.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Supabase MCP
resources.description: Supabase's official remote MCP server for docs, account, database, functions and related project tools.
resources.for_whom: Developers whose agents need to work on a Supabase project they control.
resources.access_notes: Remote URL https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp with OAuth. Can list, query and change project data. Read Supabase's MCP security notes and restrict feature groups before connecting production.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: SkillsMP
resources.description: A community index of Agent Skills scraped from GitHub. Not run by Anthropic.
resources.for_whom: People searching for community skills at their own risk.
resources.access_notes: Unvetted. Individual skills keep their upstream licences. Anonymous API is rate limited. Treat a listed skill as untrusted code until you have read it. Optional paid API plans.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Notion MCP
resources.description: Notion's hosted MCP server for searching, reading, creating and updating pages and databases in a workspace the user can access.
resources.for_whom: People whose agents need live Notion context they already have permission to see.
resources.access_notes: Remote URL https://mcp.notion.com/mcp with OAuth. Can read and write workspace content. Workspace owners can manage which clients connect. Prefer the hosted server over the unmaintained self-hosted repo.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Cloudflare MCP
resources.description: Cloudflare's hosted API MCP server covering DNS, Workers, R2, Zero Trust and the rest of the Cloudflare API, plus docs search.
resources.for_whom: People whose agents work on a Cloudflare account they control.
resources.access_notes: Remote URL https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp with OAuth, or a scoped API token as a bearer. Can change account configuration. Grant the smallest permission set. Other product-specific Cloudflare MCP URLs exist; this is the main API server.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: OmniSeek
resources.description: A local MCP add-on that searches places web search often misses, including Bilibili, Zhihu and scholarly papers.
resources.for_whom: People whose agents need those sources in Claude Code, Cursor or Codex.
resources.access_notes: Install with uv tool install omniseek, then claude mcp add omniseek -- omniseek. Runs on your computer. Apache-2.0. Python 3.11 or later.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: ECC
resources.description: An agent harness that adds planning, review, memory, skills and AgentShield security scanning to Claude Code and other coding agents.
resources.for_whom: People running Claude Code, Codex or similar who want that workflow installed once rather than restated every session.
resources.access_notes: Guided setup is npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 setup (Node.js 18 or later). Claude Code plugin is ecc@ecc from github.com/affaan-m/ECC. Install only from those official sources. Hooks run with the agent's permissions. OSS is MIT. ECC Pro GitHub App is a separate paid product for private repos.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Agent Reach
resources.description: A CLI that gives coding agents read access to platforms generic web search misses, including GitHub, YouTube, Bilibili, V2EX and login-walled social sites.
resources.for_whom: People whose agents need those sources, including Chinese platforms and logged-in feeds.
resources.access_notes: Point the agent at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Panniantong/Agent-Reach/main/docs/install.md. The PyPI package named agent-reach is a different project. Login channels copy that site's Chrome session into a dedicated local browser; they do not read the password store. Prefer a secondary account. MIT.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Ruflo
resources.description: An agent harness around Claude Code and Codex: plugins, a console, optional MCP, and coordinated multi-agent workflows.
resources.for_whom: People who want swarm, memory and policy tools on top of an existing coding agent.
resources.access_notes: Prefer npx ruflo@latest init wizard, or in Claude Code /plugin marketplace add ruvnet/ruflo. There is also curl -fsSL https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ruvnet/ruflo@main/scripts/install.sh | bash. Read the script before running it. Mods run with your account's permissions; review them before installing. MIT.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Anthropic Cybersecurity Skills
resources.description: An independent community library of 818 cybersecurity skills in the agentskills.io format, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, NIST CSF 2.0 and related frameworks. Not affiliated with Anthropic.
resources.for_whom: Security practitioners whose agents need structured playbooks for authorised testing, defence and education.
resources.access_notes: Install with npx skills add mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills. Apache-2.0. Includes offensive and dual-use techniques. Use only on systems you own or have written permission to test. A listed skill is not a security audit of your environment.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Context Mode
resources.description: An MCP server and hooks layer that sandboxes large tool output, keeps a local session index, and can run analysis scripts so agents do not dump whole files into context.
resources.for_whom: People running Claude Code or other supported clients whose context windows fill with tool output.
resources.access_notes: In Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add mksglu/context-mode then /plugin install context-mode@context-mode. MCP-only: claude mcp add context-mode -- npx -y context-mode. ctx_execute can run code on your machine. Elastic License 2.0: you may not offer it as a hosted service that exposes its features.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: agentglass
resources.description: A local desktop workspace that gathers coding-agent terminals, diffs, pull requests, approvals and a browser they can drive into one window.
resources.for_whom: People running Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or OpenCode on their own machine, often several at once.
resources.access_notes: Download from GitHub releases. macOS builds are unsigned. Data stays in local SQLite. Agents run with your permissions. It controls what they can approve, but it doesn't sandbox them. MIT.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested
